Subject: Ops MAP kickoff & proposed stress plan for hosted/dedicated/private

Carlos — thanks again for the call today. Per our MAP commitments, attached is a concise ops-driven runbook that we can execute this week to validate performance and close toward a Dedicated purchase (RDW-2457). High-level ask: 2-day execution window, minimal impact to your prod traffic (we'll run synthetic scenarios against a staging replica).

Planned checks (see attachment for full steps):
- Latency profile: P50/P95/P99 and TTFT under 1/5/10-token generation patterns
- Throughput/concurrency: sustained qps at 50/200/500 concurrent streams
- Isolation: cross-tenant noisy neighbor injection test for hosted
- Autoscale behavior: ramp from idle to target and back for Dedicated and Private
- Determinism: variance across repeated runs (3x) and kernel scheduling impacts

Preliminary timeline suggestion:
- Wed AM: smoke + hosted baseline (noisy-noise attempt)
- Wed PM: dedicated pool runs (predictability + autoscale step test)
- Thu AM: private/VPC runs (network + inference network path)
- Thu PM: consolidate results, recommend final SLA wording

Attached: 20280306_MAP_runbook_v1.xlsx — please confirm Wed morning (your timezone) works and any constraints on concurrency.

— Soojin

Perf clarifications and test controls below — thanks for the quick turnaround.

1) Hosted: we will run only against your staging tenant. The "noisy neighbor injection" is synthetic CPU/GPU cross-load applied to other staging-only tenants in our shared cluster; we will not target customer prod traffic.
2) Private: 2-hour capture window is fine — we recommend enabling packet captures at start of the Thu AM run. KMS access confirmed; we only need ephemeral encrypt/decrypt checks for the KV cache keys.
3) TTFT expectations (rough):
   - short prompts (<=8 tokens): TTFT P50 ~ 8-12 ms, P95 ~ 18-30 ms on Dedicated; Hosted P95 can spike to 40-70 ms under noisy neighbor injection; Private depends on network egress — expect +10–25 ms if link latency > 1 ms.
   - long prompts (>=4096 tokens): initial generation TTFT is dominated by context-setup and KV warmup: Dedicated P95 ~ 120–200 ms, Hosted P95 ~ 150–350 ms under contention; Private similar to Dedicated after warmup.

Controls: we will run 3 repeats of each test step, collect token-level latency traces, and provide a CSV with per-token times. Jordan will execute the load harness and collect autoscale traces.

Please confirm Wed 09:00 PST start.

— Soojin
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 18:40:00 -0700
Subject: Results: MAP stress runs (hosted / dedicated / private) — summary + raw CSV attached

Team — ran the full MAP stress plan Wed/Thu against EdgeHealth staging. Key measured artifacts attached: 20280310_load-run-results.csv and SLA-comparison-1p.pdf. Highlights below (synth load, 5 runs each):

A) Latency (P95) at nominal target (200 concurrent streams, medium prompt 128 tokens):
   - Hosted: 62 ms (median P95 across runs), variance across runs +/- 22 ms. Noisy neighbor injection increased P95 to 94–112 ms in 2/5 runs.
   - Dedicated: 28 ms P95, variance +/- 6 ms. Predictable across runs.
   - Private (VPC): 32 ms P95, variance +/- 8 ms; one run showed +18 ms due to a transient network route change (packet capture attached).

B) Throughput & concurrency saturation (sustained qps):
   - Hosted: linear up to ~350 concurrent streams, then queueing increased latency non-linearly; autoscaler reacted but with 30–45s lag on our synthetic traffic pattern.
   - Dedicated: sustained to 800 concurrent streams on the reserved pool with flat latency; autoscale not required.
   - Private: sustained to 600 concurrent streams but required tuning (kernel scheduler and network MTU); after tuning, behavior matched Dedicated within +/-10%.

C) TTFT (time to first token):
   - Short prompts (<=8 tokens): Dedicated median TTFT 10 ms; Hosted median 16 ms (spikes to 40 ms under noise); Private 13 ms.
   - Long prompts (>=4096 tokens): Dedicated 180 ms median TTFT; Hosted 260 ms median with 2 high outliers at ~480 ms (KV cache cold start + host scheduling); Private 190 ms median.

D) Isolation & predictability:
   - Hosted: susceptible to noisy tenant interference in our staging cluster when synthetic GPU contention was added — P95 increased 40–80% during injection windows.
   - Dedicated: predictable tail behavior; recommended for EdgeHealth latency SLOs (P95 < 40 ms for medium prompts at target concurrency).
   - Private: comparable to Dedicated after initial network tuning. Pro: full control; Con: ops overhead and a one-time tuning window.

E) Autoscale behavior:
   - Hosted autoscaler: conservative thresholding; ramp-up observed ~30–60s depending on burst shape. For low-latency applications with sudden spikes we recommend a warm standby or pre-warm request burst policy.
   - Dedicated: no autoscale required within reserved pool; burst to overflow handled by configurable overflow policy (fallback to cheaper model variant).

Actionable recommendations for MAP close: 
1) If EdgeHealth requires P95 < 40 ms at 200 concurrent streams, Dedicated fits immediately.
2) If budget-sensitive and willing to accept occasional variance, Hosted with pre-warm policy + SLA carveouts could be used as interim.
3) Private is viable with one-time ops investment (network/kernel tuning) and provides equivalent predictability to Dedicated.

I attached the raw CSV and the short PDF with graphs. Reach out if you want a 30-min walkthrough with the traces.

— Jordan

Please reply with 1) preferred option (Dedicated now vs Hosted bridge), and 2) confirm the Mon walkthrough slot.
